name: On Intel Arc dGPUs, llama.cpp agentic workloads stall and enabling FA can cut prompt processing ~15x
symptom: On a Ryzen 5600g with Intel Arc Pro B50 (Battlemage), agentic coding with Devstral 2 small 24b or GPT-OSS 120b stalls in the first few agent steps; prompt processing drops to single digits and effectively stops once context reaches 4k-8k tokens. Measured without FA: ~300 tok/s pp; with FA enabled: ~15-20 tok/s. SYCL is worse - black screen and OOM when context fills, with 8 GB still free on the GPU.
root_cause: Not established. The reporter tried Vulkan and SYCL, latest devel kernels and mesa 26.0, multiple llama.cpp builds including one with XE2 improvements, FA on/off, ctk/ctv q8_0 on/off, various UB/B combinations and several offloading strategies, on both Windows and Linux, with no configuration that works.
workaround: No reliable workaround reported. Intel dGPU support in llama.cpp should be treated as experimental for long-context or agentic workloads; validate on your exact SKU before committing to it.
notes: Confidence is medium: it is one user's hardware-specific report with no maintainer diagnosis, but the configuration sweep is thorough and the FA regression is quantified. The FA-on pp drop parallels gotcha-vulkan-flash-attn-slower on a different vendor's stack, which suggests FA dispatch is the thing to A/B first on any non-CUDA backend.
